c53c3b080d69.title: RL learning framework for the guided exploration of crystalline materials.
c53c3b080d69.caption: a , Schematic of the latent diffusion framework with GRPO. The process shifts from standard likelihood-driven sampling (red path) to reward-guided exploration (green path), which enables the agent (denoising diffusion models) to navigate the latent space towards underexplored regions via flexible, multi-objective optimization. b , Continuous creativity reward matrix based on AMD, which is designed to penalize known or redundant structures while maximizing rewards for unique and new compounds. c , Stability reward mapping as a function of the predicted energy above the convex hull. The function guides the agent towards thermodynamically stable phases while penalizing unstable configurations. d , t -SNE projection of structural embeddings showing 1,000 reference (training) structures (grey density contours) and 500 generated structures coloured by the diversity reward. Here, Δ E F is the formation-energy difference; C 0 , C t and C T denote the initial, intermediate and terminal crystal states, respectively; q is the forward process; and p θ is the learned reverse process.
c53c3b080d69.title_zh: 强化学习引导晶体结构探索
c53c3b080d69.caption_zh: 原文 Fig. 1 展示潜空间扩散模型与组相对策略优化（GRPO）的连接：通过新颖性、稳定性与多样性等奖励引导晶体候选探索。下方给出不同奖励的定义和分布示意，用于理解生成目标如何与材料发现目标对齐。

c53c3b080d69.title: Illustration of the policy optimization algorithm.
c53c3b080d69.caption: a , GRPO framework. b , Ablation study of the policy optimization algorithm between GRPO and the REINFORCE algorithm. Step refers to the RL step number. Solid lines indicate centred rolling mean values and shaded bands indicate rolling mean ± 1 rolling s.d. computed within the same moving window. c , Ablation study without diversity rewards in GRPO training. Solid lines and shaded bands are defined as in b . PO, REINFORCE policy optimization; w/o, without. Source data

c53c3b080d69.title: Comparison of generative models trained with the Alex-MP-20 dataset.
c53c3b080d69.caption: Performance of de novo crystal generation across models using 10,000 sampled structures. Metrics include mSUN (metastable, unique and novel fraction), uniqueness, novelty, compositional validity (using the SMACT filter), metastability (MLFF-predicted energy above the convex hull, \({E}_{\mathrm{hull}}^{\mathrm{MLFF}}\) < 0.1 eV per atom) and coverage (Fréchet materials distance, FMD − 1 ). Comp. Validity, compositional validity; w/ RL, with RL.

c53c3b080d69.title: Novelty–stability dilemma in generative modelling for materials discovery.
c53c3b080d69.caption: a , b , t -SNE projections of structural embeddings for 1,000 generated samples from the pretrained Chemeleon2 baseline ( a ) and the Chemeleon2 with RL model ( b ). Grey contours denote the reference distribution from the Alex-MP-20 dataset, and yellow points indicate structures satisfying the mSUN criterion. c , Trade-off between novelty and stability across generative models, highlighting the shift of the RL-optimized Chemeleon2 towards higher stability and novelty. Marker shape indicates the dataset used for novelty evaluation: circles, Alex-MP-20; squares, MP-20. Marker colour indicates the model: bright green, Chemeleon2; dark green, Chemeleon1; blue, MatterGen; pink, DiffCSP; yellow, ADiT. The blue-shaded region schematically illustrates the novelty–stability trade-off. d , Representative crystal structures from four characteristic regions identified in b . Source data

8c775dd0753c.title: GFF-MAP workflow for GNN-based analysis of grain-level fatigue failure and micromechanical assessment of pores.
8c775dd0753c.caption: Schematic overview of the proposed framework in which graph neural network (GNN) models receive microstructural descriptors as input and are trained on crystal plasticity simulation data. Depending on the task, the GNNs are configured to perform either regression, predicting grain-level micromechanical fields, or classification, directly identifying fatigue critical pores. The network architecture and output layers are adapted according to the prediction objective.
8c775dd0753c.title_zh: GFF-MAP：晶粒疲劳失效与孔隙微观力学分析流程
8c775dd0753c.caption_zh: 图神经网络以微观结构描述符为输入，利用晶体塑性模拟数据训练；根据任务分别回归晶粒尺度的微观力学场，或分类识别影响疲劳的关键孔隙。网络结构与输出层随预测目标调整。

fce3019b88c7.title: Fig. 2: Round-by-round performance of AI-generated T-domain variants in the minimal system producing 1 and 2.
fce3019b88c7.caption: a Production of 1 and 2 for variants tested in round 1–3, expressed in E. coli and screened in succinate XPP medium at the 1 mL scale, shown relative to the WT GxpS_T3 control included in each experiment (WT = 100%). Bars represent mean values, and error bars indicate ± standard deviation (SD) ( n = 3 biological replicates); points indicate individual replicates. Complete raw and processed datasets underlying all experiments are provided in Source Data and Supplementary Data 1 , respectively. Quantification was performed by LC-MS using external calibration with synthesized or purified standards (see Supplementary Fig. 2 ). b , Violin plots summarizing the distribution of activities for each round. Violin plots show the distribution of normalized production levels for variants tested in each design round. The shape of the violin plot reflects the probability distribution of activity values, i.e., the density of variants exhibiting that level of activity, with wider regions indicating a higher frequency of observations. Within each violin, the dashed line indicates the median and the dotted lines the 25th and 75th percentiles; the violin spans the full range of the observed values. Sample sizes are as in ( c ). c Fraction of variants exceeding the indicated activity thresholds. Sample sizes: round 1 ( n = 11), round 2 ( n = 25), round 3 ( n = 30). Source data are provided as a Source Data file.
